study_identification_part.si_4_title: Individual differences v. the average patient: mapping the heterogeneity in ADHD using normative models

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Gaussian process regression was used as a Bayesian non-parametric interpolation method for normative modeling, yielding coherent measures of predictive confidence in addition to point estimates.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: normative models were estimated using Gaussian process regression (Rasmussen and Williams, 2006), a Bayesian non-parametric interpolation method that yields coherent measures of predictive confidence in addition to point estimates.

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Regional gray matter volume and white matter volume were predicted across the brain at each voxel using voxel-based morphometry derived from T1-weighted MRI images processed with SPM12 and DARTEL.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: we estimated normative brain changes across the adult lifespan represented in our study (Fig. 1) using Gaussian process regression to predict regional gray and white matter volumes across the brain from age and sex.

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Age and sex were used as covariates/predictors in the Gaussian process regression model to predict brain structure at each voxel.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: In this study, we used covariates age and sex to predict brain structure at each voxel.
